title: Crystallization control of 2.0-eV bandgap perovskites for all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells - Nature Energy
gist: Nanjing University researchers led by Hairen Tan develop a surface reconstruction and halide homogenization (SRH) strategy for 2.0-eV ultrawide-bandgap perovskites, using solvent-induced surface reconstruction plus transient chloride incorporation from oleylammonium chloride to suppress wrinkling and reach a 1.46V open-circuit voltage, enabling monolithic all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells at 30.1% power conversion efficiency (29.3% certified) — work already patented and being commercialized via Tan's company Renshine Solar.

themes.theme: Surface reconstruction and halide homogenization mechanism

insights.claim: Ultrawide-bandgap (UWBG) perovskite performance in triple-junction solar cells has been limited by severe surface wrinkling, halide heterogeneity, and large open-circuit voltage deficits, all originating from the high bromide-to-iodide ratios these materials require.
insights.speaker: Yuhong Zhang, Enzuo Wang, Haonan Liu, Dong Zhou et al.
insights.so_what: Confirms the same bromide-driven defect problem flagged in the companion commentary as the core bottleneck blocking >30% all-perovskite triple-junction efficiency.
insights.quote: However, their performance is limited by severe surface wrinkling, halide heterogeneity and large open-circuit voltage deficits originating from high Br–I ratios.

insights.claim: The team's surface reconstruction and halide homogenization (SRH) strategy uses synergistic solvent and additive engineering — solvent-induced surface reconstruction plus transient chloride (Cl−) incorporation from oleylammonium chloride — to simultaneously regulate crystallization and eliminate stress-induced morphological disorder in 2.0-eV bandgap perovskite films.
insights.speaker: Yuhong Zhang, Enzuo Wang, Haonan Liu, Dong Zhou et al.
entities: surface reconstruction and halide homogenization strategy
insights.so_what: The named mechanism (transient Cl- incorporation via oleylammonium chloride) is the specific reproducible recipe other perovskite labs and manufacturers would need to license or replicate.
insights.quote: Through synergistic solvent and additive engineering, involving solvent-induced surface reconstruction and transient Cl− incorporation from oleylammonium chloride, surface wrinkling is suppressed, and Br/I crystallization is synchronized with promoted homogeneous halide distribution.

insights.claim: The resulting UWBG perovskite films show uniform surface potential, suppressed non-radiative recombination, improved carrier mobility, and reach an open-circuit voltage of 1.46V, a notable gain for a 2.0-eV bandgap material where voltage deficits are typically largest.
insights.speaker: Yuhong Zhang, Enzuo Wang, Haonan Liu, Dong Zhou et al.
insights.so_what: 1.46V open-circuit voltage on a 2.0-eV subcell is close to the material's theoretical ceiling, a concrete number investors can compare against future UWBG perovskite papers to judge whether this remains state of the art.
insights.quote: The resulting UWBG perovskite films show uniform surface potential, suppressed non-radiative recombination, improved carrier mobility and an open-circuit voltage of 1.46 V.

insights.claim: Integrating the improved 2.0-eV UWBG subcell with optimized 1.6-eV and 1.22-eV absorbers yields a monolithic all-perovskite triple-junction solar cell with 30.1% power conversion efficiency in-house and 29.3% independently certified efficiency, plus what the authors describe as robust operational stability.
insights.speaker: Yuhong Zhang, Enzuo Wang, Haonan Liu, Dong Zhou et al.
insights.so_what: 29.3% certified efficiency is a hard, comparable data point against silicon-perovskite tandems and other triple-junction PV efforts — the number to track for competitive benchmarking in next-gen solar.
insights.quote: Integrating this UWBG subcell with optimized 1.6- and 1.22-eV absorbers yields monolithic all-perovskite triple-junction solar cells with 30.1% power conversion efficiency (certified 29.3%) and robust operational stability

insights.claim: The authors position this result as a promising route toward all-perovskite multijunction photovoltaics exceeding 35% efficiency, framing 29.3% as an intermediate milestone rather than a ceiling.
insights.speaker: Yuhong Zhang, Enzuo Wang, Haonan Liu, Dong Zhou et al.
insights.so_what: Sets an explicit efficiency target (>35%) investors can use as a milestone marker for whether this technology roadmap is on track in future publications.
insights.quote: providing a promising route towards >35% efficient all-perovskite multijunction photovoltaics

insights.claim: A patent (ZL202610056293.8) based on this work has already been granted to Renshine Solar (Suzhou) Co., Ltd, with authors Yuhong Zhang, Haonan Liu, Renxing Lin and Hairen Tan named as inventors, meaning the IP is already commercially claimed rather than purely academic.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A granted patent assigned to a named commercial entity is a direct, actionable signal — Renshine Solar is the company to watch/diligence for commercialization of this specific triple-junction perovskite technology.
insights.quote: Patent (ZL202610056293.8) has been granted to Renshine Solar (Suzhou) Co., Ltd, based on this work, with Y. Zhang, H. Liu, R.L. and H.T. named as the inventors.

insights.claim: Corresponding author Hairen Tan is founder, Chief Scientific Officer and Chairman of Renshine Solar (Suzhou) Co., Ltd, a company explicitly described as commercializing perovskite photovoltaics — establishing a direct academic-to-startup commercialization pipeline for this research.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Tan's dual role as lead academic author and founder/CSO/Chairman of the commercializing company is the clearest investable thread in this record — worth tracking Renshine Solar's funding rounds, product roadmap, and manufacturing partnerships.
insights.quote: H.T. is the founder, Chief Scientific Officer and Chairman of Renshine Solar (Suzhou) Co., Ltd, a company that is commercializing perovskite photovoltaics.
